title: Integrals of Vector Functions; Projectile Motion
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Definite and Indefinite Integrals of Vector Functions
definitions.latex: \int \mathbf{r}(t) \, dt = \left( \int f(t) dt \right)\mathbf{i} + \left( \int g(t) dt \right)\mathbf{j} + \left( \int h(t) dt \right)\mathbf{k} + \mathbf{C}
definitions.statement: The integral of a vector function is defined by integrating each component function independently. The constant of integration C is an arbitrary vector constant in R^3.
conditions: Component functions f, g, h are integrable on [a, b]
definitions.explanation: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus applies component-wise: int_a^b r(t) dt = R(b) - R(a) where R'(t) = r(t).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Velocity integrates to position, and acceleration integrates to velocity.

definitions.title: Classical Projectile Motion Equation
definitions.statement: For a projectile launched from the origin with initial speed v_0 at inclination angle alpha subject only to downward gravitational acceleration g, the position r(t) follows a parabolic path.
definitions.explanation: Flight time T = (2 v_0 sin alpha)/g, Maximum height H = (v_0^2 sin^2 alpha)/(2g), Range R = (v_0^2 sin 2alpha)/g.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Horizontal velocity remains constant while vertical velocity decreases linearly with time.
